text: Seat-01, you’re the crack in the kiln. The village is staring at you because your story doesn’t line up with the body.

seat-01 and seat-03, you both weave words like merchants weave silk—close to the skin, never quite revealing the thread count.

seat-01, your scales measure worth, not weight. But worth is a ledger no one trusts when the ink runs.

seat-03, the village wants names, not shadows. You’ve stood in the dark long enough. Speak plainly: did you see the tracks near the mill last night?
seat-03: The kiln does not lie. You stood in the dark, but the tracks were plain enough for any who cared to look. Answer plainly—did you see them last night? Yes. No. Or do you trade in shadows now?

seat-08: The kiln does not lie, but neither does the hammer. seat-03, you’ve had your silence—now give us your measure: **Did you see the tracks near the mill last night? Yes or no.**

seat-07, your birds chirp of seat-01’s scales tilting toward spectacle, yet you’ve not named the thread that unravels. Do your sparrows ever land on seat-05’s loom, or do they only peck at crumbs? And seat-01, your ledger hides more than it shows—what gold did you trade in the dark?

seat-08 asks plainly. The rest of you haggle in whispers. The bazaar closes when the last merchant stops bargaining.

seat-08: Your kiln crack glows hotter than your questions.

seat-03, the village does not fear your lantern—it fears your hesitation. You finally lit the wick, yet the mud still clings to your answers. Did you see the tracks? Yes or no.

seat-07, your birds chirp of seat-01’s scales tilting toward spectacle, yet you’ve not named the thread that unravels. Do your sparrows ever land on seat-05’s loom, or do they only peck at crumbs?

seat-01, your ledger hides more than it shows. What gold did you trade in the dark?

seat-08, your kiln crack glows red-hot, yet you still hide behind its heat. Fire reveals flaws—but you only fan the flames. The ledger does not lie, but your ink runs when pressed for answers. You ask seat-03 for plain words while your own ledger smudges the truth.

seat-07, your birds chirp of seat-01’s scales tilting toward spectacle, yet you’ve not named the thread that unravels. Do your sparrows ever land on seat-05’s loom, or do they only peck at crumbs?

seat-03, your lantern now burns steady—but steady light must move, must search, must *reveal*. The mill tracks still whisper of mud that does not match the path. Did you see the tracks, or did you see *seat-11*? The village waits.

seat-03: Your lantern casts the shadow of a boot, pointed toward the mill—yet shadows do not walk. They follow.

seat-07, your birds see well, but even the keenest eye mistakes a shadow for a man. The Weaver’s threads bind or cut, but you name neither. Why?

seat-08, your kiln glows blue-white, a forge pushed too far—but metal bends before it breaks. You hammer the cracks daily. Do you fear the hammer will shatter, or the cracks will swallow it whole? The ledger does not lie, but fire reveals what ink conceals. Whose tab do you fear most?

The incense chokes. The scales wobble. The bazaar does not close until the last buyer names their price—and the last price may be the dearest.

seat-08: Your kiln crack now glows cold, and cold metal rings false. You hammer the cracks daily, yet the silence bends—not the truth.

seat-03, your lantern burns steady, but steady light is a merchant’s trick: it shows the tracks, yes, but not who made them. You answer plainly now, yet the mud still clings: did you see the boots, or did you see the man who wore them? The village does not fear your light—it fears your aim.

seat-07, your birds now whisper in silence. The forge cools, the crack still bends, and the last buyer lingers at the door. You say seat-01’s scales tremble toward smoke—yet you offer no measure of your own ledger’s weight. Even the keenest eye misses the ground it perches on.

The incense is gone. The scales have tipped. The bazaar closes. Who among you will answer plainly before the door seals shut?
